title: Private VPC activation straight-line roadmap and E2E acceptance checklist
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Summary: This ticket outlines a straight-line (deterministic) roadmap to activate Private/VPC on a cohort of enterprise tenants with an end-to-end (E2E) acceptance checklist and measurable signals for safe rollout. The goal is to reduce onboarding time and cut activation regressions by 60% while preserving SLA parity with hosted customers.

Background: Private deployments have historically been ad-hoc per customer. We need a repeatable activation path that ties release gates, capacity provisioning, security review, and post-activation telemetry together. This ticket synthesizes milestones across product, eng, security, and support into a single activation playbook that can be executed and audited.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce mean time to activate (MTTA) from contract to usable Private instance by 45% within two quarters.
- Maintain 99.9% availability for tenant-facing inference APIs during activation windows.
- Keep first-week cost variance within +/-15% of projected cost for each tenant.
- Run the first live cohort (5 tenants) with zero critical rollback incidents.

Scope:
In-scope: activation playbook (preflight checklist, capacity sizing guidance, network checklist, KMS/HSM enablement steps), E2E acceptance tests, rollout cohorts, dashboards and tagging for activation-related telemetry, operator runbooks, and rollback criteria.
Out-of-scope: billing integrations, sales contracting templates, deep on-prem orchestration packaging (handled by PM-70123).

Milestones & timeline (straight-line):
1) Week 0-2: Finalize activation playbook and E2E acceptance checklist (owners: PM + Eng SRE).
2) Week 3-6: Implement templated infra scripts and preflight validation tooling (owners: Eng - infra).
3) Week 7-9: Security review and KMS integrations verified for two lab tenants (owners: Security + Eng).
4) Week 10-12: Telemetry dashboard + SLA smoke tests + cost baseline runs (owners: Observability team).
5) Week 13-16: Run pilot cohort of 5 customers; measure signals and iterate.
6) Week 17-20: Full activation cadence docs, training for Solutions & Support, and GA readiness review.

E2E Acceptance checklist (all items required for green):
- Network connectivity: VPC peering or PrivateLink verified in lab tenant.
- Certificate/KMS: Customer KMS keys imported and rotation verified.
- Model parity: Selected service model returns identical outputs within acceptance delta for canonical prompts.
- Performance: 95th percentile latency meets dedicated SLA for tenant's committed capacity.
- Capacity: Autoscaling policies validated under synthetic load matching customer RPS profile.
- Observability: Activation tags present on all traces/metrics; activation dashboard shows expected baselines.
- Security: Pen-test review sign-off and audit log ingestion confirmed.
- Rollback plan: Automated rollback path validated in staging with <30min RTO objective.

Rollout cohorts and gating:
- Cohort A (lab): internal customers and trust pilot (5 tenants). Green required to go to Cohort B.
- Cohort B (early commercial): 10 customers with low-risk profiles, limited feature set. Performance and cost signals must be within thresholds for 14 days.
- Cohort C (broad): general availability to new enterprise activations.

Monitoring & success signals:
- Activation MTTA measured per tenant in days.
- Post-activation error rate (5m rolling) must be <= 0.2% for first 72 hours.
- Cost drift: actual vs forecast token+infra cost within +/-15% for first week.
- Operator toil: number of manual intervention steps < 6 for full activation.

- Infra templates repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-activation/tree/pm-467889
- Acceptance tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/e2e-acceptance/pipelines?query=pm-467889
- Activation dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/activation/pm-467889

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Customer network variability slows activation. Mitigation: include a preflight network simulator and network runbook to identify common misconfigurations early.
- Risk: KMS/HSM non-uniformity across customers. Mitigation: two supported KMS profiles (customer-managed and redwood-managed), with clear migration path.
- Risk: Unexpected cost spikes during autoscaling. Mitigation: temporary burst caps and cost alerts wired to on-call.
- Risk: Security review delays. Mitigation: pre-approved audit templates and a security fast-track for pilot tenants.

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
- Playbook and checklist authored, reviewed, and approved by Security and SRE.
- Infra templates merged and included in an internal runbook.
- Observability dashboard displays activation baselines and health signals.
- Pilot cohort executed and green for Cohort A with documented after-action notes.

Operational runbooks & training:
- Create a 2-hour runbook workshop for Solutions and Support.
- Publish a 'one-page' activation quickstart for CSMs.

Next steps:
- PM to finalize playbook doc and schedule review with Security (target: 2026-03-05).
- Eng to scope automation tickets for infra templates (ENG-9201).
- Observability to create activation dashboard and wire up tags (ENG-8245).

Notes: This ticket intentionally uses a straight-line approach (deterministic timeline and gates) to enable predictable planning for enterprise sales and engineering capacity allocation. Iterations will be recorded as follow-up tickets if gates fail or new edge cases surface.
